name: Battle of Kadesh

phases.title: The Hittites wait behind Kadesh
phases.text: Muwatalli had placed his troops behind Old Kadesh. Ramesses had been told that the Hittite army was far off, so he was with the Amun division and his bodyguard while the Re division was still coming up to the camp.
phases.when: 9 day of the third month of Shemu, Year 5

phases.title: Hittite chariots cross the river and scatter the Re division
phases.text: The Hittite chariots crossed the river and charged the middle of the Re division as it marched towards Ramesses. Caught in the open, the division scattered in all directions.

phases.title: The chariots attack the camp
phases.text: The Hittite chariotry rounded to the north and attacked the Egyptian camp through the Amun shield wall, and panic spread among the Amun division. Some of the Re division fled north to the camp, pursued by Hittite chariots.

phases.title: Ramesses charges into the Hittite ranks
phases.text: The momentum of the Hittite attack waned as chariots were impeded by obstacles in the camp. Ramesses defeated the first attackers and personally led several charges with his guard, some Amun chariots and survivors of the Re division.

phases.title: The Egyptian counter-attack drives them to the river
phases.text: The Hittites, believing their enemies routed, stopped to plunder the camp. An Egyptian counter-attack then drove them back towards the Orontes and away from the camp, and in the pursuit lighter Egyptian chariots overtook Hittite chariots.

phases.title: A second Hittite counter-attack meets new arrivals
phases.text: As the retreat reached the river, Muwatalli ordered another thousand chariots to counter-attack towards the camp. The Ne'arin from Amurru arrived and surprised them, and the Ptah division arrived from the south and threatened the Hittite rear.

phases.title: The Hittites are pinned against the Orontes
phases.text: After six unsuccessful charges the Hittite forces were almost surrounded and the survivors were pinned against the Orontes. They abandoned their chariots and tried to swim the river, and many drowned. The Hittites held on to Kadesh.

note: The Egyptians came from the south and Kadesh lay to the north, so the plan puts the Hittites north of the Orontes and the Egyptian camp south of it. The Orontes, the ford and the places of the divisions are set by judgement: the accounts name the divisions' positions only against towns (Shabtuna, Arnaim) that the plan does not draw, and do not say exactly where the camp lay. The Egyptian division of Set was marching on the road and is not drawn, as the account does not place it in the fighting. The Egyptian accounts are the main source, and a Hittite account of the outcome differs: it has Ramesses leaving in defeat.
